question: Which Hermes extension path should be probed first for Cairn recall and selected capture while preserving native memory and reusing the existing lifecycle engine?
scope: Plan a native Hermes compatibility probe and staged Cairn integration covering CLI and messaging gateways in the first release

authority_boundary.authority_source: Owner requested a Hermes integration plan, then explicitly selected CLI and messaging gateways for the first integration.
authorized_scope: Inspect current source and prior findings
Write an implementation plan; host changes are outside this planning turn

evidence.summary: The written plan recommends a native provider-plus-hook probe first and treats route acceptance, lifecycle capture completion, scope propagation and retained-context budgeting as explicit subsequent gates. Alternatives are MCP-only useful baseline and a hooks-only adapter if compaction coverage is proven. Existing provider slot and builtin memory coexistence are documented; no Hermes config or code has changed. Cairn/PostgreSQL and owned adapters are managed dependencies; model endpoints are external boundaries substituted only in native fixtures. Source lifecycle tests already cover unchanged capture and note revision for other harnesses; Hermes-specific behavior is still provisional.

evidence.summary: Installed Hermes source exposes provider registration plus real PluginContext register_hook forwarding, builtin memory alongside one external provider, pre_llm_call context injection and provider on_pre_compress. Provider prefetch skips continue; plugin hook does not share that skip. API context is stored separately as api_content, so extraction must use original content to avoid memory echo. Memory-manager shutdown drains background tasks for five seconds; lifecycle extraction may need 35 seconds. Cairn existing handle() validates Claude UUID or OpenCode IDs; Hermes requires explicit normalization and original scope labels. These are source observations, not native Hermes integration proof.

assertions.text: Installed Hermes exposes provider lifecycle plus hook registration, but prefetch filtering, retained API context and shutdown deadlines require native verification.
Probe the provider-plus-pre-turn-hook route first, then implement explicit tools, ambient recall, selected capture and deployment in validated stages. Route choice remains provisional.
alternatives: General hooks plugin with verified compaction coverage
tradeoffs: Cairn occupies the single external-provider slot
Reuse of the existing Claude selector adds capture calls but preserves shared selection behavior
Native proof is required before claiming reliable compaction or exit capture

alternatives.option: Provider plugin plus pre-turn hook, verified first

verification_criteria: Native event and context probe before adapter selection
Cross-agent continuation, compaction, session switch, no duplicate capture
Existing lifecycle regression checks and installation idempotency
Native CLI and gateway entry points both pass tools, recall, capture and compaction checks
Gateway routing, concurrent conversations, duplicate delivery, idle expiry, reconnect and graceful restart
reopening_conditions: Native callback or provider registration differs from source
Retained API context cannot be bounded using supported interfaces
An existing external provider must remain active, or a configured gateway lacks a required lifecycle callback
